clues.text: I was the priest of Bethel.
I sent a message to King Jeroboam of Israel about Amos.
I told Amos to run away to the land of Judah.
I told Amos he must no longer prophesy at Bethel.
I said Amos was conspiring against Jeroboam in the midst of the house of Israel.
I said the land could not put up with all of Amos's words.
I reported that Amos said Jeroboam would die by the sword.
I reported that Amos said Israel would surely go into exile from its land.
I called Amos a visionary and told him to earn his bread in Judah.
I said Bethel was the sanctuary of a king and the house of a kingdom.
Amos answered me that he was not a prophet nor the son of a prophet.
Amos told me Jehovah took him from following the flock to prophesy to Israel.
Jehovah's word through Amos said my wife would become a prostitute in the city.
Jehovah's word through Amos said my sons and daughters would fall by the sword.
I tried to send away a Judean visionary at Bethel's royal sanctuary.
I heard that I would die in an unclean land while Israel went into exile.
I reported to Jeroboam that Amos was conspiring against him, then forbade prophesying against the house of Isaac.
After I ordered Amos to stop prophesying at Bethel, Jehovah said my land would be apportioned with a measuring line.
I was among the sheep raisers from Tekoa.
Jehovah took me from following the flock and told me to prophesy to Israel.
I was a herdsman and took care of sycamore fig trees.
Amaziah the priest of Bethel told me to run away to Judah.
I said I was not a prophet nor the son of a prophet.
Jehovah showed me a basket of summer fruit.
My words concerned Israel in the days of Uzziah of Judah and Jeroboam son of Joash of Israel.
I received my message two years before the earthquake.
I said Jehovah will roar out of Zion and raise his voice out of Jerusalem.
When Jehovah showed me a locust swarm, I pleaded for Jacob, and Jehovah reconsidered.
When Jehovah showed me fire consuming the land, I pleaded again, and he reconsidered.
Jehovah showed me a plumb line among his people Israel.
Amaziah told King Jeroboam that I was conspiring against him.
Amaziah said Bethel was the sanctuary of a king and I must not prophesy there.
After the plumb line, Jehovah told me he would no longer pardon his people Israel.
I announced that the high places of Isaac would be desolated.
I told Amaziah Jehovah said his wife would become a prostitute in the city.
At the summer-fruit vision Jehovah said, “The end has come for my people Israel.”
I declared a famine, not for bread or water, but for hearing the words of Jehovah.
I saw Jehovah stationed above the altar and heard him say to strike the pillar.
I prophesied Jehovah would raise up the fallen booth of David.
Zechariah later recalled the earthquake in Uzziah's days that dated my words.
From Tekoa's flocks I was sent to Israel; at Bethel Amaziah tried to send me back to Judah.
Twice Jehovah reconsidered judgment when I pleaded for weak Jacob, then set a plumb line and stopped pardoning.
I faced Amaziah's ban at Bethel's royal sanctuary and answered with Jehovah's exile word on his house and on Israel.
After summer fruit marked Israel's end, I foresaw people roving sea to sea seeking Jehovah's word and not finding it.
James in Jerusalem cited my word about rebuilding David's booth among the nations.
I was among the exiled people by the river Chebar.
I saw visions of God.
I was the son of Buzi the priest.
Jehovah appointed me as a watchman to the house of Israel.
I ate a scroll, and it was as sweet as honey in my mouth.
I engraved Jerusalem on a brick and laid siege to it.
My wife died, and I did not observe mourning rites as commanded.
In a valley full of dry bones, I prophesied and they came to life.
I saw the glory of Jehovah and fell facedown.
I prophesied against Gog of the land of Magog.
My call came in the fifth year of the exile of King Jehoiachin.
I was in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar.
I saw four living creatures, each with four faces and four wings.
I saw wheels within wheels, their rims full of eyes.
Above the expanse I saw the likeness of a throne like sapphire.
Jehovah made my forehead like a diamond, harder than flint.
I went to the exiles at Tel-abib by the river Chebar.
In a dazed condition I stayed among them for seven days.
I lay on my left side 390 days for the guilt of Israel.
I lay on my right side 40 days for the guilt of Judah.
I baked my bread over cattle manure instead of human excrement.
I shaved my head and beard with a sharp sword used as a razor.
I weighed my hair into thirds for fire, sword, and wind.
I packed luggage for exile and bore a hole through a wall by hand.
I carried my belongings on my shoulder in the darkness as a sign.
I ate my bread with trembling and drank water with agitation.
Jehovah said in a single blow he would take away my dear one.
I spoke to the people in the morning, and my wife died in the evening.
Jehovah said I had become a sign for them.
I took two sticks, for Judah and for Joseph, and joined them as one.
A man who escaped from Jerusalem told me the city had been struck down.
Jehovah opened my mouth, and I was no longer speechless.
I saw a temple vision in which a man whose appearance was like copper measured the structure.
Jehovah promised through me to give a new heart and put a new spirit within his people.
I sat in my house with the elders of Judah before me when Jehovah's hand fell upon me.
Spirit brought me back to the exiles in Chaldea, and I told them everything Jehovah had shown me.
Jehovah had me set an iron griddle as an iron wall between me and the city.
Jehovah said that if I failed to warn the wicked, their blood would be on me.
Jehovah asked me if those bones could live, and I answered that he was the One who knew.
I saw the glory of Jehovah enter the temple by way of the gate that faces east.
I saw a scroll written on the front and on the back with dirges, moaning, and wailing.
In the 30th year, on the fifth day of the fourth month, the heavens were opened to me.
The hand of Jehovah came upon me there by Chebar.
Spirit entered me and made me stand up on my feet.
Jehovah said my tongue would stick to the roof of my mouth until he opened it.
I protested that from my youth no unclean meat had entered my mouth.
I wrapped a few strands of hair in the folds of my garment.
Spirit lifted me between the earth and the heavens and brought me to Jerusalem in visions.
I dug through a wall and saw detestable things practiced in the temple.
I saw a man in linen mark the foreheads of those sighing over the detestable things.
I saw the glory of Jehovah depart from over the threshold of Jehovah's house.
Jehovah told me not to cover over the mustache or eat bread brought by others when my wife died.
I prophesied to the wind, and breath entered the slain so they stood as a large army.
I said the bones are the whole house of Israel.
Jehovah said my people treat me like a romantic love song; they hear but do not act.
In the 12th year of our exile, in the tenth month, the escaped man reached me.
In my vision a man with the appearance of copper held a linen cord and a measuring reed.
I saw water going out from under the threshold of the temple toward the east.
I prophesied that Jehovah's servant David would be their king and one shepherd.
Jehovah set me down in the middle of a valley plain full of very dry bones.
I saw women sitting and weeping over Tammuz.
I saw about 25 men with their backs to Jehovah's temple, worshiping the sun.
While I was prophesying, Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died, and I fell facedown and cried out.
I went in the heat of my spirit, with Jehovah's hand strong upon me.
In my vision the temple stream rose until there was enough water to swim in.
Elders of Israel sat before me to inquire of Jehovah.
Jehovah told me to groan with bitter grief before their eyes.
I was told to recite a proverb about a cooking pot set on the fire for the rebellious house.
I prophesied as I was commanded, and as I prophesied there was a noise and bones began to come together.
I lived among the Tel-abib exiles as a mute watchman.
The morning I taught the people, my wife died that evening; I groaned in silence as a sign of the sanctuary's fall.
My mouth was opened the evening before an escapee arrived to report Jerusalem's fall.
From living creatures by Chebar to glory departing Jehovah's house, my visions tracked Jehovah's judgment.
Jehovah said he was not sending me to a people of unintelligible speech.
In my vision the name of the city from that day was Jehovah Is There.
I conceived and bore Hosea a son.
Jehovah told Hosea to marry a woman of prostitution, and he married me.
I conceived again after my first son and gave birth to a daughter.
My son was named Jezreel.
My daughter was named Lo-ruhamah.
After I weaned Lo-ruhamah, I conceived and gave birth to a son.
My second son was named Lo-ammi.
Jehovah linked my son Jezreel's name to an accounting against the house of Jehu.
I was the daughter of Diblaim.
I bore Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah, and Lo-ammi in turn, weaning one daughter between the births.
My children's names marked mercy withdrawn and “not my people,” while Jezreel named bloodshed's accounting.
I was a prophet who received a pronouncement in a vision.
I asked, “How long, O Jehovah, must I cry for help, but you do not hear?”
I stationed myself on the rampart to keep watch.
Jehovah told me the righteous one will live by his faithfulness.
I said that even if the fig tree does not blossom, I will exult in Jehovah.
I asked why Jehovah made me witness wrongdoing and tolerate oppression.
Jehovah told me he was raising up the Chaldeans, a ruthless nation.
I said Jehovah's eyes are too pure to look on what is evil.
I asked why Jehovah keeps silent when a wicked man swallows someone more righteous.
Jehovah told me to write down the vision and inscribe it clearly on tablets.
Jehovah told me that even if the vision delays, keep in expectation of it.
I prayed a prayer in dirges.
I pictured the Chaldean hauling nations with a fishhook and dragnet.
I asked whether he would keep emptying his dragnet, slaughtering nations without compassion.
I stood at my guardpost to see what Jehovah would speak by means of me.
Woe oracles I recorded include building a city by bloodshed.
I wrote that the earth will be filled with the knowledge of Jehovah's glory as waters cover the sea.
I said Jehovah is in his holy temple; be silent before him, all the earth.
I trembled within and quietly waited for the day of distress.
I said the Sovereign Lord Jehovah would make my feet like those of a deer.
I cried over unchecked violence, then wrestled with Jehovah using the Chaldeans as his tool.
From the rampart I was told to write a vision that would not lie, and that the righteous live by faithfulness.
I recorded five woes against the plunderer.
Though flock and fields fail, I vowed joy in the God of my salvation and deer-like tread on high places.
Paul and others cited my line that the righteous one will live by faithfulness.
I was a prophet who spoke Jehovah's word to Zerubbabel and Joshua.
I asked if it was time to dwell in paneled houses while Jehovah's house lay in ruins.
The people listened to me and began to show fear because of Jehovah.
I delivered Jehovah's message to the people: “I am with you people.”
With Zechariah I prophesied, and the Jews resumed building God's house.
I told the people to go up to the mountain, bring lumber, and build Jehovah's house.
Jehovah stirred up Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the people after my message, and they began to work.
I asked who among the remnant had seen Jehovah's house in its former glory.
I told Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the people to be strong and work.
I said the future glory of this house would be greater than the former.
I said they had sown much but harvested little, and wages went into a bag full of holes.
After my message, work on Jehovah's house restarted on the 24th day of the sixth month in Darius's second year.
I said Jehovah would shake the heavens and the earth and the sea and the dry land.
I asked the priests whether holiness transfers by touch, and whether uncleanness does.
From the day the temple foundation was laid, I announced Jehovah would send a blessing.
I told Zerubbabel Jehovah would make him like a seal ring.
Ezra records that through Zechariah and me the elders prospered until Jehovah's house was finished.
I rebuked paneled houses beside a ruined temple, then Jehovah stirred leaders and people to rebuild.
In Darius's second year I moved them from “not yet time” to foundation-day blessing.
Hebrews recalls my word that Jehovah would shake not only the earth but also the heaven.
I was a prophet who opposed Jeremiah in the house of Jehovah.
I broke the yoke bar off Jeremiah's neck.
I said Jehovah would break the yoke of the king of Babylon.
I died in the same year I prophesied, in the seventh month.
I was the son of Azzur from Gibeon.
I spoke in the beginning of Zedekiah's reign, in the fourth year, in the fifth month.
I said within two years Jehovah would bring back the temple utensils from Babylon.
I said Jeconiah and all the exiles of Judah would return within two years.
Jeremiah said “Amen” to my peace words, then warned that only fulfillment proves a peace prophet.
I spoke before the priests and all the people in Jehovah's house.
After I broke the wooden yoke, Jehovah said iron yoke bars would replace it.
Jeremiah told me Jehovah had not sent me, and I had caused the people to trust in a lie.
Jeremiah said I would die that year for urging rebellion against Jehovah.
I claimed that as I broke the yoke bar, Jehovah would break Nebuchadnezzar's yoke from all the nations within two years.
From Gibeon I promised a two-year end to Babylon's yoke.
I predicted that the temple vessels and Jeconiah would return.
For urging rebellion, Jehovah sentenced me to die that year, and I died in the seventh month.
I was the son of Beeri.
Jehovah told me to marry a woman of prostitution.
I married Gomer the daughter of Diblaim.
Gomer bore me a son.
Jehovah told me to name my son Jezreel.
Jehovah told me again to love an adulterous woman.
I purchased her for myself.
I prophesied during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.
My ministry also fell in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.
Jehovah told me the land had turned away from him by prostitution.
Jehovah told me Jezreel's name pointed to an accounting against Jehu's house.
Jehovah told me he would break Israel's bow in the Valley of Jezreel.
Jehovah told me to name Gomer's daughter Lo-ruhamah.
Jehovah told me to name her next son Lo-ammi.
I paid 15 silver pieces and a homer and a half of barley for her.
I told her she must remain mine and not commit prostitution.
I said Jehovah delights in loyal love, not in sacrifice.
Jehovah told me Lo-ruhamah meant he would no longer show mercy to Israel's house.
Jehovah told me he would still show mercy to Judah's house.
Jehovah said Lo-ammi meant “you are not my people.”
I said Israel would dwell long without king, prince, sacrifice, pillar, ephod, or teraphim.
I said Israel would afterward look for Jehovah and for David their king.
I announced Jehovah's legal case against the land: no truth, loyal love, or knowledge of God.
I said Jehovah's people are silenced because there is no knowledge.
I said Ephraim is like a round cake left unturned.
I said they sow wind and will reap a storm wind.
I recorded Jehovah's word: “Out of Egypt I called my son.”
I called Israel to come back to Jehovah their God.
Jehovah compared my love for an adulterous woman to his love for Israel while they turned to other gods and loved raisin cakes.
I recorded Jehovah's promise that his people would call him “My husband,” not “My Baal.”
I said Jehovah would betroth his people to himself in righteousness, justice, loyal love, and mercy.
I recorded Jehovah asking how he could give Ephraim up or treat Israel like Admah and Zeboiim.
I said Jehovah would heal their unfaithfulness and love them of his own free will.
Jesus cited my recorded words that Jehovah wants mercy and not sacrifice.
Paul cited my words about those called “Not my people” becoming “sons of the living God.”
I was a prophetess.
I was the wife of Shallum.
Josiah's men came to me to inquire of Jehovah.
I dwelt in the Second Quarter of Jerusalem.
I spoke Jehovah's reply for the king of Judah.
My husband was son of Tikvah son of Harhas.
My husband was caretaker of the wardrobe.
Hilkiah the priest was among those who spoke to me.
I said Jehovah would bring calamity on that place and its inhabitants.
I said the calamity matched the words of the book the king of Judah had read.
I said they abandoned Jehovah and made sacrifices smoke to other gods.
I said Jehovah's rage against that place would not be extinguished.
I said the king of Judah's heart was responsive and he had humbled himself.
I said the king of Judah had ripped his garments apart and wept before Jehovah.
After the book of the Law was found, I was the prophetess who answered the king of Judah's inquiry.
I gave one word of nationwide calamity and a separate word of peace for the inquiring king.
I said the king of Judah would be gathered to his ancestors and laid in his grave in peace.
I said his eyes would not see all the calamity coming on that place.
Chronicles records I spoke of all the curses written in the book they read before the king of Judah.
I was the son of Amoz.
I saw Jehovah sitting on a lofty throne.
In my vision seraphs stood above him, each with six wings.
A seraph touched my mouth with a glowing coal from the altar.
I said, “Here I am! Send me.”
My vision concerned Judah and Jerusalem.
I prophesied in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.
I met King Ahaz with a message from Jehovah.
I announced a sign: a young woman would give birth to a son named Immanuel.
I walked naked and barefoot for three years as a sign.
King Hezekiah sent messengers to me during the Assyrian threat.
I told Hezekiah to set his house in order, because he would die.
I said Jehovah would add 15 years to Hezekiah's life.
I said a cake of pressed dried figs should be applied to Hezekiah's boil.
I said Jehovah would make the shadow go back ten steps as a sign.
I wrote, “Comfort, comfort my people.”
I wrote of a voice calling out in the wilderness.
I named Cyrus in my prophecy.
In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw Jehovah.
I said I was a man of unclean lips dwelling among a people of unclean lips.
The seraph said the coal had touched my lips, and my error had departed.
Jehovah asked whom he should send, and who would go for us, and I heard him.
I took my son Shear-jashub with me to meet Ahaz.
I met Ahaz at the end of the conduit of the upper pool by the highway of the laundryman's field.
I told Ahaz not to fear Rezin and the son of Remaliah.
I called those two kings stumps of smoldering logs.
I told Ahaz that unless he had firm faith, he would not be firmly established.
Jehovah told me to tell Ahaz to ask for a sign as deep as the Grave or as high as the sky.
I took a large tablet and wrote on it with an ordinary stylus.
I wrote the name Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
I had relations with the prophetess, and she became pregnant.
I said I and the children Jehovah gave me were as signs and miracles in Israel.
My naked-and-barefoot walk was a sign against Egypt and Cush.
Eliakim, Shebnah, and the elders of the priests came to me in sackcloth.
I told them not to be afraid because of the words with which the Assyrian servants had taunted Jehovah.
I said Sennacherib would hear a report and return to his own land.
I said he would fall by the sword in his own land.
I said Jehovah would defend Jerusalem for his own sake and for the sake of his servant David.
Before I left the middle courtyard, Jehovah told me to turn back and speak again to Hezekiah.
I asked Hezekiah what the men from Babylon had said and where they were from.
I wrote that a child would be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Eternal Father, Prince of Peace.
I wrote of a twig that would grow out of the stump of Jesse.
I wrote that the wolf would reside with the lamb.
Jehovah sent me to tell this people to hear again and again but not understand.
I asked how long, and Jehovah answered until cities crash in ruins.
I said Syria and Ephraim planned to set up the son of Tabeel as king in Judah.
I said that before the boy Immanuel knew how to reject bad and choose good, the land of the two kings Ahaz dreaded would be abandoned.
I secured faithful witnesses for my tablet writing: Uriah the priest and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah.
Jehovah told me to call my son Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
I said that before my son Maher-shalal-hash-baz could call “My father!” or “My mother!,” Damascus's wealth and Samaria's spoil would be carried off.
Jehovah told me to remove the sackcloth from my hips and to take my sandals off my feet.
In the year that Ahaz died, I made a pronouncement against Philistia.
I sent word to Hezekiah after he prayed about Sennacherib's letters.
I said the daughter of Jerusalem would shake her head at Sennacherib.
I said Sennacherib would not enter the city, shoot an arrow there, or cast up a siege rampart against it.
I told Hezekiah that everything in his house would one day be carried to Babylon.
I said some of Hezekiah's own sons would become court officials in the palace of the king of Babylon.
The rest of Uzziah's history was recorded in my writings.
The rest of Hezekiah's history is written in the vision of me, the son of Amoz.
I wrote of nations beating their swords into plowshares.
I wrote of a precious cornerstone laid in Zion.
I wrote of a despised servant avoided by men.
I wrote that he would be pierced for our transgression.
I saw Jehovah in the year Uzziah died, and my prophetic vision spanned the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.
With Shear-jashub I met Ahaz at the laundryman's-field highway; later the Rabshakeh took his stand at that same place.
After Ahaz refused a sign deep as the Grave or high as the sky, I announced Immanuel.
My sons Shear-jashub and Maher-shalal-hash-baz were among the signs Jehovah gave through me.
I wrote Maher-shalal-hash-baz on a tablet before witnesses, then gave that name to the son the prophetess bore.
For three years I went naked and barefoot as a portent that captives of Egypt and Cush would go that way.
When Hezekiah's sackcloth envoys reached me, I said Sennacherib would hear a report, return, and fall by the sword at home.
I told the dying Hezekiah he would die; then, still in the middle courtyard, I was turned back to promise 15 more years.
I prescribed pressed dried figs for Hezekiah's boil and announced the shadow's ten-step return as Jehovah's sign.
After Hezekiah showed Babylon everything, I asked what they had seen, then said house and sons would go to Babylon.
I recorded Uzziah's remaining deeds, and Hezekiah's remaining history stands in my vision.
I wrote of one despised, avoided, and pierced for transgression.
I named Cyrus Jehovah's shepherd and anointed one who would fulfill Jehovah's pleasure toward Jerusalem.
I was the son of Hilkiah, of the priests in Anathoth.
Jehovah made me a prophet to the nations.
I said I was only a boy and did not know how to speak.
Jehovah touched my mouth and put his words in my mouth.
I saw the branch of an almond tree.
I saw a boiling pot, its mouth tilted away from the north.
I warned that Jehovah's house would become like Shiloh.
I wore yoke bars on my neck.
Hananiah broke the yoke bar off my neck.
I dictated Jehovah's words, and Baruch wrote them in a scroll.
King Jehoiakim burned the scroll written at my dictation.
They threw me into a cistern, and I sank down into the mud.
Ebed-melech pulled me up out of the cistern.
I bought a field in Anathoth while the city was under siege.
I told the exiles in Babylon to build houses and plant gardens.
Jehovah told me not to take a wife in that place.
In my heart Jehovah's word became like a burning fire shut up in my bones.
I chanted over Josiah, and singers kept singing about him in their dirges.
Jehovah formed me in the belly and knew me before I came out of the womb.
Jehovah made me a fortified city, an iron pillar, and copper walls.
My call began in the 13th year of Josiah.
I stood in the courtyard of Jehovah's house and spoke to those coming to worship.
After I prophesied against the temple, the priests and prophets said I must die.
Ahikam son of Shaphan supported me so I was not handed over to be put to death.
I bought a linen belt and put it around my waist, but did not dip it in water.
I hid the linen belt in a cleft of the crag by the Euphrates.
When I dug up the belt, it was ruined and completely useless.
Jehovah sent me down to the potter's house.
I bought an earthenware flask from a potter and smashed it in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom.
Pashhur struck me and put me in the stocks at the Upper Gate of Benjamin.
I told Pashhur that Jehovah had named him, not Pashhur, but Terror All Around.
I cursed the day I was born.
I said Amen to Hananiah, then warned that a peace prophet is known when his word comes true.
After my wooden yoke was broken, Jehovah said iron yoke bars would take its place.
I told Hananiah Jehovah had not sent him, and that he would die that year.
I wrote to the elders and priests taken into exile with Jeconiah.
I told them to seek the peace of the city where they were exiled.
I said Babylon's domination would last 70 years.
My cousin Hanamel asked me to buy his field in Anathoth.
I weighed out 17 shekels of silver for Hanamel's field.
I gave the purchase deed to Baruch to put in an earthenware vessel.
I was confined and unable to enter Jehovah's house, so I sent Baruch to read the scroll.
Jehoiakim ordered men to seize me and Baruch, but Jehovah kept us concealed.
After the scroll was burned, I dictated another, and many more words were added.
Officials accused me of deserting to the Chaldeans when I went out toward Benjamin.
They beat me and put me in the house of Jonathan the secretary as a prison.
While confined, I was given a loaf of bread daily from the Street of the Bakers.
In the cistern of Malchijah where they threw me there was no water, only mud.
I put worn-out rags between my armpits and the ropes.
Until Jerusalem was captured, I remained in the Courtyard of the Guard.
Nebuzaradan released me from handcuffs at Ramah.
I went to Gedaliah at Mizpah and stayed among those left in the land.
Johanan and the army chiefs took me down to Egypt as far as Tahpanhes.
At Tahpanhes I hid large stones in the mortar at the entrance of Pharaoh's house.
My word continued until the 11th year of Zedekiah, when Jerusalem went into exile.
Jehovah told me not to say I was only a boy.
Jehovah told me he was wide awake concerning his word to carry it out.
Men of Anathoth sought my life, saying I must not prophesy in Jehovah's name.
Jehovah's words were found, and I ate them, and they became the joy of my heart.
I sat alone because of Jehovah's hand.
I said woe to me, my mother, that she gave birth to me, a man of quarreling.
Jehovah told me not to enter a house where a mourners' feast was held.
Jehovah told me not to enter a house of feasting to sit and eat and drink.
I wished my head were waters and my eyes a fountain of tears.
I said I would speak no more in Jehovah's name, but I grew tired of holding it in.
I became a laughingstock all day long; everyone ridiculed me.
Pashhur was the leading commissioner in Jehovah's house when he struck me.
I prophesied that Pashhur and all in his house would go to Babylon and die there.
I brought the Rechabites into a temple chamber and offered them wine.
Jehovah showed me two baskets of figs set before his temple.
I said I had spoken Jehovah's word from Josiah's 13th year for 23 years.
Jehovah told me to take the cup of the wine of his wrath and make the nations drink.
In Jehovah's house, Hananiah told me within two years the Babylonian yoke would be broken.
Hananiah the prophet died that year in the seventh month, as I had said.
I wrote against Shemaiah the Nehelamite, who sent letters opposing me.
Hanamel was the son of Shallum my uncle.
I said houses, fields, and vineyards would again be bought in that land.
Zedekiah sent men to ask me to plead with Jehovah as Babylon's army approached.
I told Zedekiah that even if he defeated the Chaldeans, they would still burn the city.
Zedekiah secretly swore he would not put me to death or hand me over to those seeking my life.
I told Zedekiah that if he surrendered to Babylon's princes, the city would not be burned.
When princes questioned me, I answered as King Zedekiah had commanded about Jonathan's house.
Nebuchadnezzar ordered that I be looked after and that no harm be done to me.
Nebuzaradan gave me a food allowance and a gift and let me go.
The remnant asked me to inquire of Jehovah whether they should go to Egypt.
After ten days Jehovah's answer came to me: stay in the land; do not go to Egypt.
Presumptuous men said I was lying and that Baruch was inciting me against them.
I wrote calamity against Babylon in a book and gave it to Seraiah son of Neriah.
Uriah prophesied with words like mine and was killed; Ahikam kept me from the same fate.
I prophesied through Josiah, Jehoiakim, and Zedekiah until Jerusalem fell.
I bought Anathoth land as a sign of restoration while confined in the Courtyard of the Guard.
From cistern mud to Courtyard confinement, I still urged Zedekiah to surrender and live.
Bound among the deportees at Ramah, I chose to stay in Judah rather than go to Babylon.
I warned against Egypt, was forced there anyway, and buried stones as a sign of Babylon's throne.
I delivered Jehovah's promise of a new covenant written on hearts.
Zedekiah did not humble himself before me, the prophet who spoke from Jehovah's mouth.
The land kept sabbath until 70 years were fulfilled, according to Jehovah's word by my mouth.
In Cyrus's first year Jehovah stirred his spirit to fulfill the word spoken through me.
I was the son of Pethuel.
I warned that the day of Jehovah is near.
I described a locust invasion that stripped the land.
I said Jehovah would pour out his spirit on every sort of flesh.
I asked whether anything like this had happened in their days or their forefathers' days.
I said what one locust left, another kind ate.
I said grain offering and drink offering had ceased from Jehovah's house.
I said to blow a horn in Zion.
I called for a return to Jehovah with all the heart.
I said to rip apart hearts, not garments.
I said sons and daughters would prophesy.
I said everyone who calls on Jehovah's name will be saved.
I named swarming, unwinged, voracious, and devouring locusts in sequence.
I said even livestock groaned for lack of pasture.
I said Jehovah would compensate for the years his great locust army had eaten.
I said old men would dream dreams and young men see visions.
I said even male and female slaves would receive the spirit.
I said the sun would turn to darkness and the moon to blood.
I spoke of judgment in the Valley of Jehoshaphat.
I said to beat plowshares into swords and pruning shears into spears.
I said crowds, crowds are in the valley of the decision.
I said Jehovah would be a refuge for his people and a fortress for Israel.
Peter said the Pentecost outpouring was what was spoken through me.
I said the day of Jehovah is coming, a day of darkness and gloom.
I joined spirit outpouring with wonders of blood, fire, and columns of smoke before Jehovah's day.
I was the son of Amittai.
Jehovah told me to go to Nineveh the great city.
I ran away from Jehovah toward Tarshish.
I boarded a ship at Joppa.
Jehovah sent a huge fish to swallow me.
I was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
I proclaimed that in 40 days more Nineveh would be overthrown.
Nineveh's people put faith in God at my proclamation.
I was a prophet from Gath-hepher.
I paid the fare and went aboard to flee.
During the storm I was asleep in a ship's inner part.
The lot cast during a storm fell to me.
I said, “I am a Hebrew, and I fear Jehovah the God of the heavens, the One who made the sea and the dry land.”
I told mariners to throw me into the sea so it would calm.
I prayed to Jehovah from a fish's belly.
Jehovah commanded a fish, and it vomited me onto dry land.
After I fled the first time, Jehovah's word came to me a second time.
I went to Nineveh in obedience the second time Jehovah sent me.
Jehovah spoke through me concerning restoring Israel's boundary
Through me that boundary stretched from Lebo-hamath to the Sea of the Arabah.
Mariners learned I was fleeing Jehovah because I had told them.
I said weeds were wrapped around my head in the deep.
I prayer to Jehovah my God, I said salvation is from Him.
Nineveh was a walking distance of three days when I went there.
I walked a day's journey into Nineveh proclaiming a message from Jehovah.
God reconsidered the calamity he announced through me and did not bring it.
Jehovah sparing Nineveh was highly displeasing to me.
I said I fled because I knew Jehovah is compassionate and merciful.
I asked Jehovah to take my life; it was better to die than live.
I sat east of the city under a shelter to see what would happen.
Jehovah provided a bottle-gourd plant to shade my head and relieve my misery.
I was very pleased with a bottle-gourd plant.
A worm attacked my bottle-gourd plant, and it withered.
After experiencing a scorching east wind and the sun beating down on my head, I again said it was better to die than live.
Jehovah asked if I was right to be so angry over a certain bottle-gourd plant.
I told God that I have a right to be angry, so angry that I want to die.
Jesus said that the Son of man would be in the heart of the earth just as I was in the belly of the huge fish.
Jesus said Nineveh's men would rise in the judgment because they repented at my preaching.
Jehovah's word to Israel came through me.
I recorded Jehovah's charge that priests presented polluted food on his altar.
I recorded Jehovah's question: “Will a mere human rob God?”
I said Jehovah was sending his messenger to clear up a way before him.
I recorded Jehovah's promise to send Elijah the prophet.
I recorded the dispute “How have you shown us love?” answered with Jacob and Esau.
I said they presented blind, lame, or sick animals as sacrifices.
I said they called Jehovah's table something to be despised.
I said they were robbing God in the tithes and the contributions.
I said to bring the entire tithe into the storehouse.
I said Jehovah invited them to test him regarding the tithe blessing.
I spoke of a book of remembrance for those fearing Jehovah.
I said the sun of righteousness would shine with healing in its rays.
I said they sniffed scornfully and called the service tiresome.
I said the cunning one vowed a sound animal then sacrificed a blemished one.
I said the lips of a priest should safeguard knowledge.
I said Jehovah acted as witness against those dealing treacherously with the wife of their youth.
I recorded Jehovah's word: “I hate divorce.”
I said they weary Jehovah by asking, “Where is the God of justice?”
I said the messenger of the covenant would come to his temple.
I said he would sit as a refiner and cleanser of silver.
I said Jehovah would make those who fear him a special property.
I said you will again see the distinction between a righteous person and a wicked person.
I said to remember the Law of Moses commanded at Horeb.
I said Elijah would turn fathers' hearts back toward sons, and sons' toward fathers.
I recorded Jehovah's charge that Judah had married the daughter of a foreign god.
I said the day is coming that will burn like a furnace.
I came from Moresheth.
Jehovah's word came to me concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
I prophesied in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.
I said a ruler would come out of Bethlehem Ephrathah.
I declared what Jehovah requires: exercise justice, cherish loyalty, and walk in modesty with God.
I said Zion would be plowed up as a field.
I said Samaria would become a heap of ruins of the field.
Because of the coming plague I wailed and howled.
I walked barefoot and naked in mourning.
I said Jerusalem would become heaps of ruins.
I said the mountain of the house of Jehovah would become like high places in a forest.
I said nations would beat their swords into plowshares.
I said each one would sit under his vine and under his fig tree.
Against false prophets I said night would come with no vision.
I said those prophets proclaim “Peace!” when fed, but declare war when they get nothing.
I said, “I am filled with power by the spirit of Jehovah, and with justice and might.”
I said I tell Jacob his revolt and Israel his sin.
I said leaders judge for a bribe, priests instruct for a price, and prophets practice divination for money.
People preached at me: “Stop preaching!”
I said if a man preached about wine and alcoholic drink, he would be just the preacher for this people.
I presented Jehovah's legal case before the mountains.
I said the daughter of Zion would go as far as to Babylon and there be rescued.
Elders later recalled my Hezekiah-era warning that Zion would be plowed as a field.
In Hezekiah's day my words led the king to fear Jehovah, so Jehovah changed his mind about the calamity.
From Moresheth I foresaw both Samaria's ruin and a ruler from little Bethlehem.
I opposed prophets who practiced divination for money.
I received a vision concerning Nineveh.
My pronouncement was against Nineveh.
I said Jehovah takes vengeance against his foes.
I declared Jehovah is good, a stronghold in the day of distress.
I said distress would not arise a second time.
I said the worthless one would never pass through Judah again.
I pictured Nineveh's war chariots racing madly through the streets.
I said the gates of the rivers would be opened and the palace dissolved.
I asked where the lair of lions was, where the young lions feed.
I cried woe to the city of bloodshed.
I said Jehovah of armies is against Nineveh.
I said on the mountains are the feet of one bringing good news, proclaiming peace.
I said Nineveh was like a pool of waters, but now they are fleeing.
I asked if Nineveh was better than No-amon by the Nile canals.
I said Ethiopia was No-amon's source of boundless strength, also Egypt.
I said Nineveh's fortifications are like fig trees with the first ripe fruits.
I addressed the king of Assyria: your shepherds are drowsy.
I said all who hear the report about Nineveh will clap their hands.
I was an Elkoshite, and I told Judah to celebrate its festivals.
I paired the lion's lair emptied with the city of bloodshed never without prey.
I measured proud Nineveh against fallen No-amon and found no healing for Assyria's wound.
My message was what the Sovereign Lord Jehovah says regarding Edom.
I declared judgment against Esau's mountainous region.
I said Edom did violence to his brother Jacob.
I said Edom's presumptuousness had deceived him.
I said Edom resided in the retreats of the crag.
I said even if Edom nested among the stars, Jehovah would bring him down.
I said on the day strangers took Jacob captive, Edom acted like one of them.
I said Edom should not have gloated over his brother's day of misfortune.
I said the day of Jehovah against all the nations is near.
I said Edom's allies would deceive him and place a net under him.
I said Jehovah would destroy the wise ones out of Edom.
I said Teman's warriors would become terrified.
I said Edom should not have stood at the crossroads to slaughter escapees.
I said the house of Jacob would become a fire and the house of Esau like stubble.
I said saviors would go up on Mount Zion to judge Esau's mountainous region.
Much of my vision condemns Edom for its conduct when Jerusalem fell.
I tied Edom's crag pride to the same measure returning on his own head.
I said saviors would ascend Mount Zion and the kingship would become Jehovah's.
I was the son of Immer.
I was a priest.
I was the leading commissioner in the house of Jehovah.
I struck Jeremiah the prophet.
I put Jeremiah in the stocks.
I listened while Jeremiah prophesied.
The stocks I used were at the Upper Gate of Benjamin in Jehovah's house.
The following day I released Jeremiah from the stocks.
Jeremiah told me Jehovah had renamed me Terror All Around.
Jeremiah said I had prophesied lies.
Jeremiah said I would become an object of terror to myself and to all my friends.
Jeremiah said my friends would fall by the sword while my eyes looked on.
Jeremiah said I and all who live in my house would go into captivity.
Jeremiah said I would go off to Babylon and die there.
Jeremiah said I would be buried in Babylon with all my friends.
As Immer's son and temple commissioner, I answered Jeremiah's temple preaching with stocks.
After I freed him, Jeremiah renamed me Terror All Around and sentenced my household to Babylon.
I both struck Jehovah's prophet and prophesied lies to my friends.
I was a prophet, the son of Berechiah son of Iddo.
I prophesied alongside Haggai to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem.
With Haggai I supported Zerubbabel and Jeshua rebuilding God's house.
I saw visions in the night.
I saw Joshua the high priest standing before Jehovah's angel.
I delivered Jehovah's word to Zerubbabel: not by a military force, nor by power, but by Jehovah's spirit.
I urged the people to return to Jehovah, who promised to return to them.
I saw a man riding on a red horse among the myrtle trees.
I saw four horns that dispersed Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem.
Jehovah showed me four craftsmen.
I saw a man with a measuring line going to measure Jerusalem.
I saw Joshua clothed in filthy garments.
I said: Let a clean turban be put on Joshua's head.
I saw a lampstand entirely of gold with two olive trees beside it.
I said Zerubbabel's hands laid the foundation of Jehovah's house and would finish it.
I was told to put a crown on Joshua's head.
My night vision came on the 24th day of Shebat in Darius's second year.
I heard that the whole earth was quiet and undisturbed.
In my vision an angel asked how long Jehovah would withhold mercy after 70 years of indignation.
I heard Jerusalem would be inhabited as open rural country.
I heard Jehovah would become a wall of fire all around her.
I saw Satan standing at Joshua's right hand to resist him.
I heard Jehovah was bringing in his servant Sprout.
I saw a flying scroll 20 cubits long and 10 cubits wide.
I saw Wickedness sitting inside an ephah container.
I saw four chariots coming from between two copper mountains.
I was told to make a crown from silver and gold brought by the exiles.
I said Zion's king would come humble, riding on a donkey.
In Darius's day I joined Haggai so Zerubbabel and Jeshua restarted the temple.
From myrtle-tree horsemen to a measuring line, my night visions answered Zion's 70-year indignation.
I saw Joshua's filthy garments removed.
I told Zerubbabel the work was by spirit, not force, and that his hands would finish what they began.
I was the son of Cushi.
My line runs through Gedaliah, Amariah, back to Hezekiah.
I prophesied in the days of Josiah son of Amon.
I said the great day of Jehovah is near and approaching very quickly.
I said Jehovah would completely sweep away everything from the surface of the ground.
I said Jehovah would stretch out his hand against Judah and Jerusalem.
I said Jehovah would wipe out every vestige of Baal.
I warned those who bow down on the rooftops to the army of the heavens.
I said that day is a day of fury, distress, storm, darkness, and thick gloom.
I urged the meek of the earth to seek Jehovah, righteousness, and meekness.
I said Jehovah would make Nineveh desolate, as dry as a desert.
I condemned those who pledge loyalty to Jehovah while pledging loyalty to Malcam.
I said Jehovah would carefully search Jerusalem with lamps.
I targeted the complacent who say Jehovah will not do good and will not do bad.
I said there would be an outcry from the Fish Gate and a wailing from the Second Quarter.
I said Moab would become like Sodom and the Ammonites like Gomorrah.
I called Jerusalem a rebellious, polluted, oppressive city.
I said Jehovah would change the language of the peoples to a pure language.
I said Jehovah would allow a humble and lowly people to remain.
In Josiah's reign I warned of a day of fury, distress, storm, darkness, and thick gloom.
I tied rooftop star worship and Malcam double loyalty to a lamp-search of complacent Jerusalem.
From sweeping the ground clean I moved to a remnant calling on Jehovah shoulder to shoulder.
